rounds.text: Catvision Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 0.47x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.42x [E2, E7]. This valuation gap is further highlighted by a P/E ratio of 16.49x, which sits below the sector benchmark of 18.13x [E6]. While the company has faced long-term stagnation, recent performance indicates a sharp operational turnaround with profit growth of 254% over the trailing twelve months and 33% over the last three years [E20, E21]. This momentum is confirmed by the scanX signal engine, which notes that profit growth is currently exceeding price growth by 268%, suggesting the market has yet to price in this fundamental improvement [E49, E63]. Investors are also being paid to wait, as the stock offers a substantial dividend yield of 10.60% [E4]. Conceded: the company has struggled with long-term sales growth, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -8% and a 5-year growth rate of 0% [E14, E15, E55].
